title: Factorized path × Mirror address
hypothesis: A factorized path identity plus support-inferred Mirror role generalizes to held-out path-role pairs and uses fewer actual serialized N=20 bytes than storing independent modules for each combination, while matching a Routing Networks composition control.
physical_object: shared 2-layer modular graph with four physical modules per layer
mirror_coordinate: path factor (discrete route ID) × support-inferred role angle factor
logical_multiplicity: unseen combinations of known module paths and role views
controls: PathNet path-only with development-selected default role
Routing Networks style path and role selection among existing transforms
independent per-task full matrix upper reference

development.path_default_role_selection: min dev query MSE per path
development.role_inference: select among six candidates using support MSE

success_gate: Every fresh world on held-out pairs: factorized Mirror NRMSE <=1.10x Routing Networks control; actual N=20 bytes below flat per-combination full modules; intervention recovers path and role factors independently.
failure_gate: Any quality/byte/identifiability miss, or Routing Networks matches Mirror at equal/fewer bytes and compute.
boundaries: Do not treat 24 path-role combinations as independent capacity.
No learned router training or natural task claim.
